original_question: If K is a scattered Valdivia compact space that contains the ordinal interval [0, ω1], is there a bounded linear extension operator from C([0, ω1]) to C(K)? More generally, does C([0, ω1]) embed into C(K)?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.10: the paper asks whether a scattered Valdivia compactum containing [0,ω1] admits an extension operator from C([0,ω1]) into C(K), and more generally whether C([0,ω1]) embeds into C(K). This is the exact statement your draft is trying to capture. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem almost verbatim: it has the correct class of compact spaces (scattered Valdivia), the correct obstruction space ([0,ω1]), and the same two-part structure as the paper—first the extension-operator question, then the broader embedding question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: Make explicit that [0,ω1] means the ordinal interval endowed with its order topology, sitting inside K as a homeomorphic subspace. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

State what C(L) denotes: the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on L with the supremum norm. The paper uses C(K)-space notation without re-explaining it in Problem 5.10, so a stand-alone version should say this. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Define 'extension operator' explicitly as a bounded linear operator E:C([0,ω1])→C(K) satisfying E(f)|[0,ω1]=f for every f, after identifying the embedded copy of [0,ω1] in K. The paper says 'linear extension operator' and leaves the standard meaning implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Clarify that 'does C([0,ω1]) embed into C(K)?' means a Banach-space isomorphic linear embedding, not merely a topological embedding and not necessarily an isometric one. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

To stay paper-faithful, keep both hypotheses 'scattered' and 'Valdivia': the paper notes that the problem has a negative answer if either assumption is dropped. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
refined_question: Let K be a scattered Valdivia compact Hausdorff space, and suppose that K contains a subspace A homeomorphic to the ordinal interval [0,ω1] with its order topology. Writing C(L) for the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on L with the supremum norm, must there exist a bounded linear extension operator E:C(A)→C(K) such that E(f)|A=f for every f∈C(A)? More generally, must C(A)≅C([0,ω1]) admit a Banach-space isomorphic embedding into C(K)?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Section 5, Problem 5.10, not a broader neighboring question. The nearby context begins with Problem 5.1 (Godefroy’s problem for C(K)-spaces), explains why the Valdivia case reduces to compacta containing [0,ω1] via the Deville–Godefroy and Alster observations, recalls Theorem 5.8 as the obstruction coming from C([0,ω1]), and then states Problem 5.10. Remark 5.11 explains why a positive answer to Problem 5.10 would feed back into Problem 5.1, and Example 5.12 shows that the formulation should not be broadened by dropping either 'scattered' or 'Valdivia'. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
